## `virtualization.partition.cpu.count`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `virtualization.partition.cpu.count` | UpDownCounter | `{vcpu}` | The number of virtual processors of the specified type currently allocated to the firmware partition. [1] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.partition` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[1]:** Reports the current virtual processor allocation for the partition. In IBM Z PR/SM (classic mode) this maps to the processor-count-* fields on the logical-partition or partition object in the HMC Web Services API. Analogous to `mainframe.partition.cpu.virtual.count` in the mainframe namespace.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`virtualization.partition.id`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-partition-id) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | Unique identifier for the hardware or firmware partition. [1] | `LPAR01`; `PRODZ` |
| [`virtualization.partition.cpu.type`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-partition-cpu-type) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The category of processor type allocated to the firmware partition. [2] | `cp`; `ifl`; `icf` |

**[1] `virtualization.partition.id`:** Identifies the partition within its virtualization platform (`virtualization.platform.id`); the pair identifies it globally. The value MUST be the same for every observer of the partition. On IBM Z and LinuxONE this is the logical partition (LPAR) name, which the HMC Web Services API, z/OS RMF (SMF type 70 `SMF70LPM`) and Linux on IBM Z (`/proc/sysinfo` `LPAR Name`) all report.

**[2] `virtualization.partition.cpu.type`:** Identifies the processor type being counted. Use `all` for the total count across all processor types.

---

`virtualization.partition.cpu.type` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `aap` | Application Assist Processor (zAAP) — a specialty IBM Z processor for Java workloads, deprecated in z13 and later models. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `all` | Aggregate across all processor types allocated to this partition. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `cbp` | Container Based Processor (CBP) — a processor type for container-based workloads on IBM Z, available with SE versions 2.14.0 through 2.15.0. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `cp` | Central Processor (CP) — the general-purpose IBM Z processor type. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `icf` | Internal Coupling Facility (ICF) — a processor type used for sysplex coupling on IBM Z. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `ifl` | Integrated Facility for Linux (IFL) — a processor type optimised for Linux workloads on IBM Z. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `iip` | z Integrated Information Processor (zIIP) — a specialty engine for eligible Java and DB2 workloads on IBM Z. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `unknown` | Processor type is not known or the platform does not differentiate by processor type. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |

## `virtualization.partition.cpu.is_capped`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `virtualization.partition.cpu.is_capped` | Gauge | `1` | Indicates whether processor capping is enabled for the firmware partition (0=false, 1=true). [2] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.partition` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[2]:** When capping is enabled the partition cannot exceed its allocated processor count or scheduling weight ceiling regardless of spare capacity on the platform. In IBM Z PR/SM this corresponds to the `is-processing-weight-capped` field on the logical-partition or partition object in the HMC Web Services API (all modes). Equivalent concepts exist on VMware vSphere (CPU limit), KVM (cputune quota), and Hyper-V (processor bandwidth limits).

**[3] `virtualization.partition.id`:** Identifies the partition within its virtualization platform (`virtualization.platform.id`); the pair identifies it globally. The value MUST be the same for every observer of the partition. On IBM Z and LinuxONE this is the logical partition (LPAR) name, which the HMC Web Services API, z/OS RMF (SMF type 70 `SMF70LPM`) and Linux on IBM Z (`/proc/sysinfo` `LPAR Name`) all report.

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[3]:** Reports the total processor execution time accumulated by the partition since last activation or metrics reset. The `virtualization.partition.cpu.type` attribute discriminates by processor specialisation type (ifl, cp, icf, etc.). Analogous to the cumulative CPU time counters exposed by Linux cgroups (`cpuacct.usage`) or Kubernetes pod metrics (`container_cpu_usage_seconds_total`). No confirmed direct HMC Web Services API source has been identified for this metric; implementations should derive the value from hypervisor- level CPU timer data where available.

## `virtualization.partition.cpu.utilization`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `virtualization.partition.cpu.utilization` | Gauge | `1` | The fraction of time processors allocated to the firmware partition were busy executing work, as a ratio from 0 (idle) to 1 (fully utilised). [4] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.partition` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[4]:** Reports CPU utilization for a hardware or firmware enforced partition such as an IBM Z logical partition (LPAR) managed by PR/SM (Processor Resource/Systems Manager). Unlike `virtualization.vm.cpu.utilization`, this metric applies to partitions managed at the firmware level rather than by a software hypervisor. In IBM Z PR/SM (classic mode) this maps to the processor-usage fields in the logical-partition-usage metric group from the HMC Web Services API. The `virtualization.partition.cpu.type` attribute breaks down utilization by processor specialisation type (cp, ifl, icf, iip, etc.). Analogous to `mainframe.partition.cpu.utilization` in the mainframe namespace.

## `virtualization.partition.cpu.weight`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `virtualization.partition.cpu.weight` | Gauge | `1` | The processor scheduling weight assigned to the firmware partition. [5] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.partition` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[5]:** The weight determines the proportion of available processor cycles allocated to this partition relative to other partitions when spare capacity is available. Higher weights grant proportionally more CPU time under contention. In IBM Z PR/SM the weight is an integer in the range 1–999 set on the logical partition or partition object via the HMC Web Services API properties `initial-processing-weight`, `minimum-processing-weight`, `current-processing-weight`, and `maximum-processing-weight` (all modes). On IBM Z, the mainframe refinement of this metric adds `mainframe.partition.weight.type` to distinguish the weight categories.

**[8] `virtualization.partition.id`:** Identifies the partition within its virtualization platform (`virtualization.platform.id`); the pair identifies it globally. The value MUST be the same for every observer of the partition. ## `virtualization.partition.state.code`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `virtualization.partition.state.code` | Gauge | `1` | The operational state of the firmware partition encoded as a numeric gauge (1=in this state, 0=not in this state). [7] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.partition` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[7]:** Reports the current lifecycle state of the partition. For each partition, exactly one state value will be 1 at any given time; all others will be 0. This encoding enables Prometheus alerting rules and state-change detection without label-value cardinality issues. In IBM Z PR/SM (classic mode) this maps to the status field reported by the HMC Web Services API for the logical partition object. Valid state values are defined by the `virtualization.partition.state` attribute enum (active, not_activated, stopped, unknown). Analogous to `mainframe.partition.status.code` in the mainframe namespace.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`virtualization.partition.id`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-partition-id) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | Unique identifier for the hardware or firmware partition. [10] | `LPAR01`; `PRODZ` |
| [`virtualization.partition.state`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-partition-state) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The operational state of the partition. [11] | `active`; `not_activated`; `stopped` |

**[10] `virtualization.partition.id`:** Identifies the partition within its virtualization platform (`virtualization.platform.id`); the pair identifies it globally. The value MUST be the same for every observer of the partition. On IBM Z and LinuxONE this is the logical partition (LPAR) name, which the HMC Web Services API, z/OS RMF (SMF type 70 `SMF70LPM`) and Linux on IBM Z (`/proc/sysinfo` `LPAR Name`) all report.

**[11] `virtualization.partition.state`:** The state whose membership is being reported. One record per state value is emitted per partition; the value is 1 for the current state and 0 for all others.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `stopped` | Partition has been deactivated. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
